analysis: Docs-only PR. docs/developer/test.md head 177-203 adds the opt-in ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests (real-model SSD restore TTFT under cross-tenant contention, isolated ephemeral cache, env -i invocation). It relates to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache/TTFT oracle) as a test only. The test measures restore vs cold timing for performance and is gated by an env var. Its report retains timing samples from benchmark fixtures, not production prompts. Line 3 is a date stamp. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md patch line 119 documents provider-staged imports using host zero buffers (cbv2HostZeros) and skipping eval/stream fences to avoid evalLock. Zero source bytes can briefly commit up to one 64 MiB segment outside the MLX allocator. This is a memory-accounting/availability note (T-016/T-029-ish, A-001 KV residency T-028), not a confidentiality change. Destinations start zeroed, so no residual-data exposure is implied. Source files are not supplied: CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift and CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift (evaluateUnavailable). A later pass should verify three things. First, the shared zero buffer is never written to, which would leak or corrupt across tenants. Second, skipping fences cannot expose destinations before the copy completes. Third, the uncharged 64 MiB transient commit is bounded per concurrent import. No concrete regression is evident from the docs.
